newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open firmer, 2-yr note auction ahead.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open firmer, 2-yr note auction ahead.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened higher on Tuesday but analysts foresaw another session of narrow-ranged trading before Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
"I expect more narrow-ranged trading ahead of Greenspan although we're proably in the lower end of the range," said Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A.
Stiles said that on the eve of the Greenspan testimony, the Treasury's $17.5 billion in two-year note sale this afternoon would end up mainly in the hands of dealers.

"The market has known for quite a while that bidding on the two-year notes would take place a day ahead of Greenspan, putting more of the burden on dealers to buy them," said Stiles. "It shouldn't be news to anybody today that this two-year auction will go primarily into dealers' hands. Investors have gone into a shell before Humphrey-Hawkins and yet there is this supply that has to be taken down," he said.
Bids for the two-year notes are due at 1300 EST/1800 GMT.
Stiles pointed to a little bit of swap-related buying in short coupons as well as some "very small" central bank selling as features of overnight activity.
"There was not much out of Japan, but bunds did better. Sterling did better," said Stiles. The latter two factors could account for the firmer New York open, he said.
In early dealings, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 3/32 to 99-22/32, yielding 6.65 percent. Two-year notes were unchanged at 100-1/32, yielding 5.85 percent.
The two-year notes to be sold this afternoon were yielding 5.8625 percent in when-issued trade.
Several pieces of economic data are due on Tuesday. Most of them will attract some attention but are highly unlikely to move the market substantially.

The BTM/Schroders weekly retail sales survey is due at 0900 EST/1400 GMT. In the week ended February 15, it rose 1.7 percent. The Redbook survey of chain and department store sales is due at 1455 EST/1955 GMT. In the week ended February 15, it rose 2.8 pct.
The Conference Board's February consumer confidence measure is due at 1000 EST/1500 GMT. It is expected to edge down to 116.1 from 116.8 in January.
Also at 1000 EST/1500 GMT, the government releases figures on January import and export prices.
"It doesn't look like there's a whole lot that could move things," said one trader.
Stiles said the Treasury market is watching the dollar.
"The dollar doesn't seem to have stabilized enough," he said. "There's some concern about that."
The dollar opened mixed in New York.
But the stock market's tone has improved, as evidenced by Monday's rally, Stiles said.
At the short end of the maturity range, three-month bill rates were down one basis point to five percent. Six-month rates were unchanged at 5.01 percent.
Trading on a when-issued basis, the five-year notes to be sold on Wednesday were yielding 6.1575 percent.
Ten-year notes were up 3/32 to 99-3/32, yielding 6.37 percent.
